items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: made recordings with Eddie Condon for Columbia Recording Company

ctx.x: Or were you anxious to get back into the grove of Buck and Bubbles?
No, I wasn't anxious to do nothing but carry on as far as I could.

After that, see, we go to England to do the West End, then we come back doing the part with some of the people out of the show of the Ziegfeld Follies from "Transatlantic Rhythm," we come back in '36, that's the time we made the first broadcast for television on BBC, you know, in '36 and made recordings with Eddie Condon for Columbia Recording Company and we played all the cinemas over there.
